purpose: Diphenhydramine is most commonly used to relieve allergy symptoms like sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes, and hives. It is also widely used as a short-term sleep aid and to treat mild symptoms of motion sickness. Doctors sometimes recommend it to relieve itching from insect bites or minor skin irritations as well.
how_it_works: Your body releases a chemical called histamine when it reacts to allergens like pollen or pet dander, and histamine is what causes those uncomfortable allergy symptoms. Diphenhydramine works by blocking the receptors in your body that histamine normally attaches to, which helps calm down those reactions. Because it also crosses into the brain, it causes drowsiness — which is why it doubles as a sleep aid but also why you feel so sleepy after taking it.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is significant drowsiness or feeling groggy. You may also notice a dry mouth, dry eyes, blurred vision, difficulty urinating, constipation, or dizziness. Some people, especially children, can have the opposite reaction and feel restless or hyperactive.
warnings: Do not drive or operate heavy machinery while taking this medication because it can seriously impair your alertness and reaction time. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can intensify the drowsy effects. Use with great caution in older adults, as it can cause confusion, falls, and memory problems in seniors. Do not use it if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, or severe breathing problems without talking to your doctor first. Do not give it to children under 2 years old without a doctor's guidance.
typical_dosing: For adults and children 12 and older, the usual dose is 25 to 50 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, but no more than 300 mg in one day. For sleep, a single 50 mg dose at bedtime is typical. For children 6 to 11 years old, the usual dose is 12.5 to 25 mg every 4 to 6 hours. Always follow the package instructions or your doctor's advice, and only use it for short periods of time.
